title: Adaptive or periodically corrected low-rank AdamW for small LM training
useful_signal_summary: Medium scale barely passed at about 1.049x AdamW validation loss with 56.7%-62.5% optimizer-state ratio, and the no-residual ablation failed catastrophically. claim_scope: Synthetic Numpy attention-cache reconstruction probe over 30 seeds, length 1024, dimension 128, and 128 queries: adaptive sparse fp16 residual gates on top of a 2-bit KV cache improve over a plain 2-bit base and random residual allocation, but are consistently worse than simple uniform 3-bit quantization at the same 3.0 bits/scalar budget.

do_not_overclaim.disclaimer: These are not validated papers, not peer-reviewed results, and not publication-positive Enoch corpus artifacts. This entry preserves bounded local evidence that may be useful for larger-compute follow-up.

followup.hypothesis: Replacing fp16 sparse residual entries with low-bit block-coded residuals or token-block precision upgrades can preserve the adaptive-gating benefit while amortizing metadata and beating uniform 3-bit KV quantization at no more than 3.0 effective bits/scalar.
required_evidence: Evaluate on real or recorded transformer KV traces, not only synthetic K/V tensors.
Compare against uniform 3-bit quantization at equal or lower effective bits/scalar including metadata overhead.
Report attention-output MSE or perplexity plus decode-time overhead for at least a small pretrained transformer.
followup.stop_condition: Stop if the gated residual format fails to beat uniform 3-bit on paired real-trace metrics, or if metadata/decode overhead pushes effective budget above 3.0 bits/scalar.
followup.success_threshold: At <=3.0 effective bits/scalar including metadata, the gated low-bit/block residual cache must reduce attention-output MSE by at least 20% versus uniform 3-bit on real KV traces and avoid a top-1 attention match regression.
followup.title: Low-bit block residual gates for 2-bit KV cache

recommended_next_action: Stop this fp16 sparse-residual variant as a proxy early falsification; the only worthwhile bounded next test is a low-bit or block-coded residual gate that must beat uniform 3-bit quantization at no more than 3.0 effective bits/scalar on real or recorded KV traces.
scale_limits: No end-to-end language model, no real transformer KV activation traces, no perplexity/task evaluation, no GPU kernel or decode-latency measurement, and no metadata-overhead implementation. The result is an early mechanism/proxy falsification of this residual format rather than a full deployment validation.

title: Adaptive Precision Residual Gates for 2-bit KV Cache
useful_signal_summary: Adaptive residual gates select useful entries: proxy and oracle residual gates reduce attention-output MSE by about 43% versus a 2-bit base, while random residual allocation reduces MSE by about 7%. However, uniform 3-bit quantization reduces MSE by about 89% at the same 3.0 bits/scalar budget and beats both adaptive residual variants on 30/30 paired seeds.

stop_reason: Bounded direct validation, not a proxy-only smoke test, falsified the practical success threshold: rank-anchor failed to outperform a simple memory-matched stride-anchor baseline at both tested cache budgets.
title: Adaptive rank-anchor KV compression on GPT-2-small-class long-prefix decoding
useful_signal_summary: Direct continuation-loss validation found that stride anchors were substantially better than adaptive anchors and rank-anchor at equal cache budget. At 25% cache, rank-anchor delta CE vs full was +0.9795 versus +0.3949 for stride; at 50% cache, rank-anchor was +0.6875 versus +0.1485 for stride. Rank-anchor beat stride on 0/64 samples at both budgets.

followup.hypothesis: If the conditional aggregator is used during training to route or reweight examples toward specialized tickets, then ticket specialization will become learnable enough to beat dense and uniform aggregation baselines on heterogeneous medium tasks.
required_evidence: Implement a true adaptive training loop where gate outputs alter ticket loss weights or minibatch assignment during training.

claim_scope: In a deterministic local Python simulator with 8 fixed seeds, 2000 writes per seed, 800-key workload, and 300 targeted adversarial persistence attacks per scheme per seed, a per-revision anchored Merkle KV trace ledger detected all targeted tampering tested and reduced median historical point verification hash work from 1334.75 operations for a hash-chain baseline to 12.0 operations.

do_not_overclaim.disclaimer: These are not validated papers, not peer-reviewed results, and not publication-positive Enoch corpus artifacts. This entry preserves bounded local evidence that may be useful for larger-compute follow-up.

followup.hypothesis: A persistent sparse Merkle tree or Merkle-B-tree trace ledger can retain the same targeted tamper-detection guarantees while closing most of the write-throughput gap to the hash-chain baseline and surviving crash/restart validation.
required_evidence: Implementation of an optimized persistent authenticated KV structure that avoids full revision snapshots
Fixed-seed adversarial suite with >=10000 writes, >=16 seeds, and the same hash-chain and plain snapshot baselines
Crash/restart test that persists state and anchors to disk, corrupts local files, reloads, and verifies current and historical queries
Write throughput, storage growth, current audit cost, historical revision audit cost, and historical point proof cost
Ablation retaining only latest anchors to confirm historical-anchor necessity
followup.stop_condition: Stop negative if any targeted attack is undetected, clean historical verification fails, crash/restart corruption is not detected, median point verification exceeds 10% of hash-chain replay, or write throughput remains below 25% of hash-chain after one optimized implementation pass.
followup.success_threshold: Across >=16 seeds and >=10000 writes per seed, optimized Merkle KV detects 100% of targeted adversarial persistence attacks, clean historical queries pass, median historical point verification remains <=2% of hash-chain replay hash work, and write throughput is at least 50% of the hash-chain baseline.
followup.title: Optimized Persistent Merkle KV Ledger With Crash-Restart Adversarial Persistence

recommended_next_action: Stop this run as no-paper useful evidence; next, implement an optimized persistent sparse Merkle tree or Merkle-B-tree ledger and rerun the same adversarial suite at >=10000 writes, >=16 fixed seeds, and with crash/restart persistence checks.
scale_limits: Synthetic single-process workload only; no real agent traces, crash/restart validation, concurrent writers, external transparency service, signatures, or optimized persistent tree. The simulator stores full revision snapshots and recomputes roots on writes, making write throughput about 9.4x slower than the hash-chain baseline and preventing a systems-performance claim.

sources.title: Internal Enoch project: Adversarial Persistence Test for Incremental Merkle KV Agent Trace Ledger

stop_reason: Medium local evidence supports the persistence mechanism but not publication readiness because the workload is synthetic, the implementation is an unoptimized simulator, the 5000-write attempt exposed harness scalability limits, and no crash/restart or real trace validation was performed.
title: Adversarial Persistence Test for Incremental Merkle KV Agent Trace Ledger
useful_signal_summary: Mechanism support: immutable per-revision Merkle root anchors preserve adversarial persistence for mutable KV trace state under targeted value-edit, deletion, rollback, replay, and forged-root attacks, while providing much cheaper historical point verification than hash-chain replay. The no-history-anchor ablation failed clean historical verification, confirming that historical anchors are necessary for the target ledger behavior.

title: Gradient Lottery Validation for Volunteer Training
useful_signal_summary: High-gradient volunteer examples often concentrated mislabeled or contradictory samples. Across 180 paired full-run comparisons, gradient lottery trailed random by 0.1711 mean accuracy with approximate 95% CI [-0.2030, -0.1391]; under clean labels it was indistinguishable from random, while under 20-40% label noise it trailed random by 0.2575 mean accuracy.

claim_scope: In a deterministic synthetic slot-valued factual QA audit, a claim-level unsupported-claim ledger localized unsupported slot-value claims across three small models and three fixed seeds better than answer-level and lexical baselines.

do_not_overclaim.disclaimer: These are not validated papers, not peer-reviewed results, and not publication-positive Enoch corpus artifacts. This entry preserves bounded local evidence that may be useful for larger-compute follow-up.

followup.hypothesis: On natural evidence-and-claim benchmarks, claim-level ledgers will improve unsupported-claim localization F1 by at least 0.10 over answer-level and lexical baselines without relying on synthetic slot exact matching.
required_evidence: At least two public natural factuality datasets such as FEVER, SciFact, HealthVer, or Climate-FEVER with evidence passages and claim support/refute labels.
An independent verifier, such as a cached/downloadable NLI model or blinded LLM adjudicator, separated from the claim generation and gold-label construction.
Fixed seeds, answer-level and lexical baselines, shuffled-evidence control, and per-dataset/per-model metrics.
followup.stop_condition: Stop negative if the ledger fails to beat the best baseline by 0.10 absolute F1 on either dataset or if independent verification shows precision below 0.75.
followup.success_threshold: Claim-ledger unsupported/localization F1 exceeds both answer-level and lexical baselines by >=0.10 absolute on each dataset, with bootstrap 95% CI lower bound above the best baseline on pooled claims.
followup.title: Natural Evidence Claim-Ledger Audit with Independent Verification

recommended_next_action: Run a natural-claim follow-up on FEVER/SciFact-style evidence with an independent verifier or human-labeled claim support labels; stop here for paper gating because this run is synthetic slot-oracle evidence only.
scale_limits: 36 synthetic source items, 972 generations, 1,823 scored slot-valued claims; small cached models only; labels and ledger rely on a controlled value universe, not independent open-domain semantic adjudication.

stop_reason: No-paper closure: medium synthetic evidence supports the mechanism, but the verifier is not independent of the controlled slot-value labeling and does not validate open-domain unsupported claims.
title: Hard Unsupported-Claim Ledger Audit Across Models
useful_signal_summary: The ledger reached F1 1.000 on scored slot-valued claims, while answer-level baseline F1 was 0.570, lexical baseline F1 was 0.190, and shuffled-context control F1 was 0.406. The controlled mixed ablation showed the localization advantage: ledger F1 1.000 vs answer-level F1 0.500.

claim_scope: In a synthetic local trace simulator, externally anchored public hash chains and verifier-keyed HMAC chains detected byte-level action/observation log edits, deletions, reorders, recompute rewrites, and fake appends, while no tested ledger detected false observation content that was logged consistently from the beginning.

do_not_overclaim.disclaimer: These are not validated papers, not peer-reviewed results, and not publication-positive Enoch corpus artifacts. This entry preserves bounded local evidence that may be useful for larger-compute follow-up.

followup.hypothesis: A real agent loop with independently signed tool invocation and output records will reject injected false final-report claims that a hash chain alone cannot detect, while preserving acceptable local overhead.
required_evidence: Implement a tool wrapper that signs command, exit code, stdout/stderr digest, timestamp, and previous ledger head before the agent can modify records.
Run at least 100 real local agent/tool episodes with controlled injected false claims, deletions, reorders, rewrites, and fake appends.
Compare rejection rate, false rejection rate, and wall-clock overhead against public unanchored and anchored-only ledger baselines.
followup.stop_condition: Stop as negative if signed observation capture cannot distinguish false claims from true claims above 80% detection at less than 20% overhead, or if integration requires unavailable private infrastructure.
followup.success_threshold: Detect at least 95% of injected false final-report claims and 100% of byte-level ledger tampering with less than 10% median wall-clock overhead on local tool episodes.
followup.title: Signed Observation Recorder for Real Agent Evidence Ledgers

recommended_next_action: Run a direct real-agent deepen test with an independent signed observation recorder; stop this run as a synthetic useful-signal result rather than paper-ready validation.
scale_limits: Synthetic traces only; no live LLM agent, real tool wrapper, remote timestamping, append-only service, trusted execution, or production adversary model. Benchmarks are local Python construction throughput, not deployment overhead.

claim_scope: On a deterministic synthetic benchmark with 96 signed poison shards per seed and five fixed seeds, lexical semantic nearest-neighbor scanning improves recall over normalized exact signatures, but the tested exact-plus-semantic hybrid does not improve over semantic-only TF-IDF and fails several held-out adversarial paraphrase styles.

do_not_overclaim.disclaimer: These are not validated papers, not peer-reviewed results, and not publication-positive Enoch corpus artifacts. This entry preserves bounded local evidence that may be useful for larger-compute follow-up.

followup.hypothesis: A stronger neural embedding or cross-encoder detector combined with exact signed-shard matching can recover at least 0.80 held-out adversarial paraphrase recall at validation precision >= 0.95 and exceed the semantic-only detector by at least 0.05 F1.
required_evidence: Run the same fixed-seed benchmark with sentence embedding and cross-encoder semantic detectors.
Compare exact-only, neural-semantic-only, and exact-plus-neural hybrid scanners using identical threshold tuning.
Report per-attack recall for indirect, distractor_wrap, semantic_gap, and obfuscated held-out paraphrases.
Add one non-synthetic or public trace-derived poison/paraphrase set if available locally without private data.
followup.stop_condition: Stop if the neural hybrid still matches semantic-only performance or if semantic_gap/obfuscated recall remains below 0.25 at the precision constraint.
followup.success_threshold: Mean held-out recall >= 0.80 at validation precision >= 0.95, with hybrid F1 at least 0.05 above semantic-only and nonzero recall on every held-out attack family.
followup.title: Neural semantic detector ablation for signed-shard paraphrase poison scanning

recommended_next_action: Stop this run as no-paper evidence; a bounded deepen follow-up should replace lexical TF-IDF with a stronger semantic detector and require a clear lift over semantic-only matching on the same held-out attack families.
scale_limits: Synthetic poison shards and generated paraphrases only; no public poisoned corpus, production retrieval traces, neural embedding models, LLM paraphrase adversary, or end-to-end downstream model harm reduction were tested.

claim_scope: On a fixed 120-task held-out local subset, 60 MBPP test tasks plus 60 HumanEval tasks, Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B-to-7B confidence routing improves over small-only and often over random matched-rate routing, but raw minimum generated-token logprob is weaker than mean or p05 logprob routing ablations.

followup.hypothesis: Less outlier-sensitive confidence scores such as mean logprob, p05 logprob, or min-k average logprob will outperform raw minimum-token logprob for 1.5B-to-7B Qwen2.5-Coder cascade routing at matched weighted cost.
required_evidence: Full local HumanEval and MBPP test-set pass@1 for small-only, big-only, random cascade, min-logprob, mean-logprob, p05-logprob, and min-k-average routers
Calibration/test split with thresholds selected only on calibration tasks and reported on held-out test tasks
Matched escalation-rate and matched parameter-weighted-cost comparisons with fixed random seeds
Mechanism diagnostics including AUC for small-model failure and recoverable failure
followup.stop_condition: Stop if no robust confidence score beats raw min-logprob by at least 2 pass@1 points at matched weighted cost, or if gains disappear under calibration/test thresholding.
followup.success_threshold: A robust confidence score improves held-out pass@1 by at least 5 percentage points over random routing and at least 2 points over raw min-logprob at the same parameter-weighted cost on combined MBPP/HumanEval.
followup.title: Robust logprob confidence scores for Qwen2.5-Coder cascade routing

recommended_next_action: Stop this minimum-token-logprob follow-up as no-paper evidence; branch to a bounded robust-confidence routing test using full local MBPP/HumanEval with calibration/test thresholds.
scale_limits: Medium subset only; deterministic pass@1 only; parameter-weighted generated-token proxy instead of measured serving cost; no calibration/test threshold split; no EvalPlus or hidden tests.

stop_reason: Medium direct evaluation did not confirm minimum-token logprob as the preferred router; stronger ablation scores beat it on pass@1 and AUC at comparable escalation rates.
title: Held-out MBPP/HumanEval confirmation for minimum-token-logprob Qwen2.5-Coder cascade routing
useful_signal_summary: Minimum token logprob is predictive of failures but not the best cascade score. Combined low-score AUC for small-model failure was 0.708 for min, versus 0.797 for mean and 0.784 for p05. At 50% escalation, min reached 75.83% pass@1 at 91.88% weighted cost versus 80.00% at 85.62% for mean and 80.83% at 87.59% for p05.

claim_scope: On 240 held-out 20 Newsgroups test passages across three fixed seeds, an order-sensitive token LCS window localizes constructed natural copied suffixes within 100 characters while rejecting shuffled-token no-copy controls at threshold 0.70.

do_not_overclaim.disclaimer: These are not validated papers, not peer-reviewed results, and not publication-positive Enoch corpus artifacts. This entry preserves bounded local evidence that may be useful for larger-compute follow-up.

followup.hypothesis: For continuations generated by a small language model after controlled exposure to source passages, order-sensitive suffix localization will retain low shuffled-control false acceptance and locate copied suffix starts substantially better than exact find and unordered token overlap.
required_evidence: Train or fine-tune a small GPT-2-class model on a controlled subset of source passages with held-out negative passages.
Generate continuations from prompts that can induce copying and label source suffix offsets from the training subset.
Evaluate exact find, unordered token overlap, local alignment, and ordered-token LCS with predeclared thresholds on copied outputs and topic-matched no-copy controls.
Report per-seed localization within 25 and 100 characters, copy accept rate, false accept rate, and examples of failure modes.
followup.stop_condition: Stop as negative if model-generated continuations do not produce enough labeled copying events for evaluation or if order-sensitive localization cannot beat exact find and unordered overlap under the predeclared accept/reject thresholds.
followup.success_threshold: Across at least three fixed seeds, ordered-token LCS or a stronger order-sensitive method should achieve at least 0.80 accepted-copy localization within 100 characters with shuffled/topic-matched false accept rate at or below 0.05, and beat exact find by at least 0.20 absolute on noisy or partial copies.
followup.title: Model-generated copy suffix localization with controlled exposure

recommended_next_action: Run the same accept/reject and localization diagnostic on actual language-model continuations with controlled source exposure before considering a bounded paper claim.
scale_limits: Queries are constructed suffixes with synthetic whitespace, truncation, character-noise, and shuffled controls; this does not test real model-generated memorized continuations, larger corpora, paraphrastic copying, adversarial near-duplicates, or production-scale retrieval.

useful_signal_summary: A medium benchmark with fixed seeds, ablations, and real baselines shows that unordered token overlap is confounded by shuffled controls, while an order-sensitive token LCS diagnostic cleanly separates copied suffixes from shuffled controls and localizes copied suffixes within 100 characters.

claim_scope: On three fixed 300-example SQuAD validation samples with google/flan-t5-small, a deterministic evidence-ledger validator can attach context-sentence evidence to many supported sub-1B generated answers and nearly eliminates true ledger validity under shuffled evidence, but the ledger prompt does not improve generation over a plain prompt.

followup.hypothesis: With constrained Evidence/Answer decoding or a more instruction-following sub-1B model, model-authored evidence quotes can achieve ledger-valid rate at least 0.70 on held-out QA while matching plain-prompt F1 within 0.02 and keeping shuffled-context ledger-valid rate below 0.05.
required_evidence: At least three fixed held-out seeds with 300 or more examples each
Plain prompt, constrained ledger prompt, shuffled-context ablation, and real extractive QA baseline
Report model-authored quote-found rate separately from any deterministic validator fallback
Ledger-valid rate, answer EM/F1, acceptance precision/recall, and shuffled-context false-valid rate
followup.stop_condition: Stop negative if the model-authored quote-found rate remains below 0.75 or ledger F1 is more than 0.05 below plain F1 on two fixed seeds.

recommended_next_action: Stop this run as no-paper evidence; a bounded follow-up should test constrained model-authored evidence ledgers with a more instruction-following sub-1B model and no deterministic quote fallback.

claim_scope: On a 5-seed sklearn digits residual-MLP experiment with row-wise ternary quantization and fp32 residual output-row preservation, selecting preserved channels by Hutchinson Hessian-trace estimates did not improve quantized accuracy over no preservation or simple controls.

do_not_overclaim.disclaimer: These are not validated papers, not peer-reviewed results, and not publication-positive Enoch corpus artifacts. This entry preserves bounded local evidence that may be useful for larger-compute follow-up.

followup.hypothesis: For sub-2-bit transformer weight quantization, preserving a small fraction of residual channels selected by calibration activation magnitude reduces held-out perplexity degradation more reliably than Hessian-trace, weight-norm, or random selection.
required_evidence: GPT-2-small-class or comparable small transformer language-model quantization run
Held-out perplexity or zero-shot metric comparison for no preservation, random, activation magnitude, weight norm, and Hessian trace
At least 3 seeds or checkpoints with identical preservation budgets
Ablation over at least 5%, 10%, and 20% preserved residual channels
followup.stop_condition: Stop if activation-magnitude preservation fails to beat random and no-preservation baselines on mean held-out perplexity degradation across 3 seeds/checkpoints.
followup.success_threshold: Activation-magnitude preservation beats all listed controls by at least 10% relative reduction in quantization-induced perplexity degradation at one or more preservation budgets, with no worse result at the other budgets.
followup.title: Activation-Magnitude Residual Channel Preservation for Sub-2bit Transformer Quantization

recommended_next_action: Stop this Hessian-trace run as a bounded early falsification; if continuing locally, branch to a separate activation-magnitude residual preservation test on a GPT-2-small-class language-model quantization benchmark.
scale_limits: Small residual MLP and image-classification digits data only; not transformer language modeling, not production packed sub-2-bit kernels, and not a full parameter-Hessian LLM study.

claim_scope: Synthetic causal-attention traces with planted periodic far-anchor motifs: exact anchor retention plus tiered quantized centroids preserves full-cache attention outputs for anchored far recalls at roughly 6% KV memory, compared with memory-matched random-anchor and segment-compression baselines.

followup.hypothesis: In a small pretrained causal LM, exact sink/local/periodic anchors plus tiered compressed centroids will preserve long-context retrieval accuracy and perplexity better than memory-matched random anchors or segment-only compression at the same KV memory budget.
required_evidence: Implement HAKV, random-anchor, segment-only, and local-window KV policies in a small pretrained transformer inference path.
Measure perplexity on real text at multiple context lengths and KV memory budgets.
Measure synthetic needle or key-value retrieval accuracy where answer evidence appears at anchored and non-anchored old positions.
Report decode latency and cache memory versus full KV and memory-matched baselines.
Include ablations over anchor stride, local window, and centroid quantization tier.
followup.stop_condition: Stop if HAKV does not beat both memory-matched controls on retrieval accuracy, or if perplexity degradation exceeds 25% relative to full KV at all tested memory budgets.
followup.success_threshold: At a KV memory ratio of 10% or less, HAKV should improve long-range retrieval accuracy by at least 20 absolute percentage points over both random-anchor and segment-only baselines while keeping perplexity degradation within 10% relative to full KV on the tested small model.
followup.title: Real-model HAKV inference fidelity on small pretrained transformers

recommended_next_action: Run a bounded real-model inference follow-up in a small pretrained transformer, measuring perplexity/retrieval accuracy, KV memory, and decode latency against memory-matched random-anchor and segment-compression controls.
scale_limits: No pretrained language model, perplexity, downstream task accuracy, production decoding throughput, or kernel-level cache-update overhead was tested. The result is a mechanism probe, not full transformer validation.
